meta.description: Cleanup of expired, outstanding authorization messages from the credit card authorization database by deleting outdated entries.
meta.process_description: The program iterates through all Pending Authorization Summaries in the IMS database and checks for each associated detail entry whether the authorization has exceeded the configured expiration date. Expired detail entries are deleted, with approved and rejected authorizations corrected accordingly in the summary counters and amounts. If after cleanup a summary contains neither approved nor rejected authorizations, the parent summary record is also deleted. The process runs as a nightly or periodic batch job with configurable checkpoint intervals for restart/recovery capability.

files.PAUTSUM0: IMS segment: Summary record of pending authorizations per account (contains counters and amounts for approved/declined authorizations)
files.PAUTDTL1: IMS segment: Detail record of an individual pending authorization (contains date, amount, response code)
files.CIPAUSMY: Copybook: Data structure for the authorization summary record (Pending Authorization Summary)
files.CIPAUDTY: Copybook: Data structure for the authorization detail record (Pending Authorization Detail)

business_rules: A pending authorization is considered expired when the difference between the current date and the authorization date is greater than or equal to the configured expiry value (default: 5 days).

When deleting an expired detail record, the counters and amounts in the parent summary record are updated: approved entries (response code '00') reduce the approval counter and amount, while all other entries reduce the rejection counter and amount.
A summary record is deleted only when both the approved authorization counter and the rejected authorization counter have dropped to zero or below (fully cleaned-up account).
The batch job sets IMS checkpoints at configurable intervals to enable a restart without data loss or duplicate processing in the event of a program failure.
If the expiry parameter is not provided as a numeric value, a default of 5 days is applied as a safety net.
On any database error (read or delete), the program terminates in a controlled manner with return code 16 to prevent data inconsistencies.
At the end of processing, the program outputs a complete processing statistics report (summary and detail records read/deleted) for audit and monitoring purposes.

variables.name: DEBUG-OFF
variables.description: Condition value indicating that debug mode is disabled (value 'N' = No). Used in production to suppress the output of diagnostic and trace information, thereby optimizing the performance of the cleanup run.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Unused filler byte in the input parameter record (SYSIN), presumably serving as a separator or alignment field between the debug flag and additional parameters. Has no independent functional significance in the cleanup process.

variables.name: PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY
variables.description: Group structure for the summary record of a pending authorization per account (included via COPY CIPAUSMY). Contains all cross-account counters and amounts for approved and declined authorizations, as well as account master data such as credit limit and balance. This record is updated after each deletion of a detail entry and is itself deleted when an account has been fully cleaned up.

variables.name: PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS
variables.description: Group structure for the detail record of an individual pending authorization transaction (included via COPY CIPAUDTY). Contains all transaction-specific information such as authorization date, card number, transaction amount, and response code. This data is used to determine whether the authorization has exceeded the configured expiration age (default: 5 days) and therefore qualifies for deletion.

variables.name: IO-PCB-MASK
variables.description: Placeholder mask for the IMS I/O Program Communication Block (PCB). Required for communication with the IMS database system, particularly for general input/output operations such as setting checkpoints for the batch job's restart/recovery mechanism.

variables.name: PGM-PCB-MASK
variables.description: Placeholder mask for the IMS Program Communication Block (PCB) of the database program interface. Used for database access to the IMS segments PAUTSUM0 (summary records) and PAUTDTL1 (detail records), and returns the status code after each DL/I operation, which the program uses to detect errors and, in the event of a database error, terminate in a controlled manner with return code 16.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA controls the entire cleanup process for expired credit card authorizations: it initializes the job, iterates through all accounts with outstanding authorizations, deletes outdated entries, and finally outputs a processing summary.

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.description: Initializes the cleanup run by determining the current date, loading the control parameters from the batch input, and validating them against acceptable values – ensuring the job starts with clearly defined processing rules.

paragraphs.name: 1000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of paragraph 1000, which serves as the structural endpoint of the batch job's initialization section and signals the return to the calling control flow.

paragraphs.name: 2000-FIND-NEXT-AUTH-SUMMARY
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the next pending authorization summary record from the IMS database in order to check the associated account for expired authorizations. Controls processing progress and handles end-of-data conditions or database errors.

paragraphs.name: 2000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of processing block 2000, ensuring a controlled return from the main processing loop of the authorization cleanup.

paragraphs.name: 3000-FIND-NEXT-AUTH-DTL
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the next pending authorization detail record for the current account and evaluates whether additional authorizations remain for expiry checking or whether processing of the account is complete.

paragraphs.name: 3000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of the processing loop over all summary records. This paragraph serves as the structural endpoint to which control returns after each loop iteration.

paragraphs.name: 4000-CHECK-IF-EXPIRED
paragraphs.description: Checks whether an individual pending authorization has exceeded the configured expiry date, and if expired, updates the counters and amounts in the parent summary record of the account accordingly.

paragraphs.name: 4000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of the processing loop over the summary records. Serves as a structural return point so that the batch process can proceed in an orderly manner to the next summary after each iteration.

paragraphs.name: 5000-DELETE-AUTH-DTL
paragraphs.description: Physically deletes a single expired authorization detail record from the IMS database, logs the success, or aborts in a controlled manner upon a database error to prevent data inconsistencies.

paragraphs.name: 5000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of the expired authorization cleanup process. This paragraph serves as the structural endpoint of the program logic and enables a clean return from the processing flow.

paragraphs.name: 6000-DELETE-AUTH-SUMMARY
paragraphs.description: Deletes the fully cleaned-up summary record of an account from the IMS database when no approved or declined authorizations remain. This step completes the account cleanup and keeps the database free of outdated entries.

paragraphs.name: 6000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of the cleanup process, serving as a structured return point for the parent processing flow and signaling the orderly termination of the batch job.

paragraphs.name: 9000-TAKE-CHECKPOINT
paragraphs.description: Sets an IMS checkpoint to permanently save the current processing state of the cleanup. This allows the batch job to be restarted at this point without data loss or duplicate processing in the event of an abend.

paragraphs.name: 9000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of the cleanup program, signaling the orderly program completion after all pending authorizations have been fully processed.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND
paragraphs.description: This paragraph controls the controlled emergency abort of the cleanup job in the event of critical database errors. It signals a severe error to the parent job scheduler to prevent data inconsistencies in the credit card authorization database.

paragraphs.name: 9999-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of the program, serving as a structured return point for the entire cleanup process. It marks the regular end of processing after all expired authorizations have been fully cleaned up.
